_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Togo covering Ewe, Kabye, and other peoples, Slave Coast trade, German Togoland, French and British mandates, Sylvanus Olympio assassination, Gnassingbé dynasty (Africa's longest ruling family), and contemporary politics.

religion.note: Vodun (Voodoo) originated in West Africa; Togo is a centre of Vodun practice; many Christians and Muslims also practise Vodun

ethnic_groups.name: Ewe
ethnic_groups.notes: Southern Togo; Gbe-speaking; cross-border with Ghana (Volta Region); partitioned by colonial borders; fishing, farming; Lomé area; historically opposition politics

ethnic_groups.name: Kabiyé (Kabyè)
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern Togo (Kara); Gnassingbé family's ethnic group; military and political dominance since 1967; terrace farming

ethnic_groups.name: Mina (Guin)
ethnic_groups.notes: Coastal; Gbe-speaking; related to Ewe; historically involved in coastal trade; Aneho area

ethnic_groups.name: Tem (Kotokoli/Cotocoli)
ethnic_groups.notes: Central Togo (Sokodé); Muslim majority; caravan trade heritage; Kotokoli kingdom

ethnic_groups.name: Tchamba
ethnic_groups.notes: Central Togo; linked to Chamba of Nigeria/Cameroon; farming

ethnic_groups.name: Moba
ethnic_groups.notes: Far north (Dapaong); farming; cross-border with Burkina Faso

ethnic_groups.name: Bassar (Bassari)
ethnic_groups.notes: Central Togo; famous traditional iron smelting; Bassar region

ethnic_groups.name: Konkomba
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern Togo; farming; cross-border with Ghana; historically marginalised

ethnic_groups.name: Lamba/Losso
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern (Kara region); Gur-speaking; warriors; related to Kabiyé

ethnic_groups.name: Akposso (Akposo)
ethnic_groups.notes: Central plateau; farming; cocoa and coffee; distinct language group

ethnic_groups.name: Other
ethnic_groups.notes: Ana, Ifè (Yoruba-related), Adja, Ouatchi, Nawdm, Gourma (Gurma), Akebu, Ntcham, and others; 40+ ethnic groups total

country_profile.notes_unique: Narrow country stretching 579 km from the Gulf of Guinea to the Sahel; the Batammariba mud tower-houses (Tata Somba) are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

natural_resources.notes: Major phosphate producer (4th in Africa historically, deposits depleted from peak); Lomé port is West Africa's deep-water continental hub (transhipment); agriculture employs 65% of population (coffee, cocoa, cotton); clinker/cement production for region.

military.notes: Forces Armées Togolaises (FAT); military dominated politics (Gnassingbé dynasty since 1967); deployed in Sahel counter-terrorism; growing jihadist threat in northern Savanes region; French military cooperation; ECOWAS mediator role.

infrastructure.notes: Togocom, Moov (Maroc Telecom) telecoms; fibre backbone; Port of Lomé connectivity.

debt_aid.notes: Lomé port drives transit trade economy for landlocked neighbours; CFA franc zone (BCEAO); Gnassingbé family in power since 1967; PND (Plan National de Développement); growing security costs from Sahel jihadist spillover.

education.notes: French language of instruction; free primary education since 2008; north-south education gap; gender gap narrowing; Koranic schools alongside secular; University of Lomé overcrowded (~70,000 students); PASEC assessments.

diaspora_migration.notes: Historical migration to Ghana (Ewe cross-border community); traders across West Africa; protest-related emigration (2005, 2017 political crises); diaspora contributes to political opposition; Nana Benz market women historical trading class.
diaspora_migration.immigration_policy: ECOWAS free movement; northern displacement from Sahel threat

digital_economy.mobile_money_adoption: Growing rapidly (Flooz by Moov, T-Money by Togocel)
tech_hubs: Lomé (Woelab, first FabLab in West Africa)
digital_economy.notes: Woelab famous for building 3D printer from e-waste; TogoFirst.com economic information portal; Togocel and Moov Africa operators; ACE submarine cable (Lomé landing); digital ID system; e-government services expanding.

country_profile.national_anthem: Terre de nos aïeux (Land of Our Forefathers)

geography.terrain: Coastal lagoons and marshes; Togo Mountains (north-south chain); savanna plateau (center/north); Mono River plain
geography.notes: Narrow country (50-150 km wide, 560 km long); Togoville (historical capital on Lake Togo); phosphate mining; Port of Lomé (only deep-water port in West Africa).

economy_extended.notes: Phosphate exporter (#5 globally); Port of Lomé (only deep-water port in region, transshipment hub); clinker/cement manufacturing; Gnassingbé dynasty (father-son since 1967); PND 2018-2022 development plan.

health.notes: Universal health insurance introduced (INAM); traditional medicine prevalent; maternal mortality high; healthcare improving slowly.

food_agriculture.notes: Subsistence farming dominates; yam production significant; coffee/cocoa in Kpalimé plateau; cotton in north; food self-sufficiency improving.

energy.notes: Nangbéto Dam (shared with Benin); CEET utility; imports electricity from Ghana/Nigeria; Blitta solar plant; energy access programme accelerating.

transport.national_airline: ASKY Airlines (pan-African, HQ Lomé, Ethiopian Airlines affiliate)
major_seaports: Port of Lomé (only deep-water port in West Africa, transshipment hub)
transport.notes: Port of Lomé (transshipment hub, Bolloré/MSC); ASKY Airlines (regional success); limited railway; motorcycle transport (zémidjans) ubiquitous.

unesco_sites_list: Koutammakou, the Land of the Batammariba
tourism.notes: Koutammakou (Tamberma Valley, one of West Africa's most unique sites); Voodoo culture; Akodessewa Fetish Market (Lomé, voodoo); transit/port city Lomé.

human_rights_gender.notes: Gnassingbé dynasty (over 50 years); 2024 constitutional amendment (parliament-elected president, opposition outcry); protests repressed; abolished death penalty (2009).

security_stability.notes: Sahel security threat spreading south (Burkina Faso border); 2024 constitutional reform crisis; history of political instability; peacekeeping contributor.

cultural_heritage.media_landscape: TVT state; mostly state-controlled; some private radio; press restrictions
cultural_heritage.notes: Voodoo heartland (alongside Benin); Koutammakou (Tamberma tower houses unique architecture); Akodessewa Fetish Market; Ewe/Kabye cultural duality.

legal_system.legal_tradition: Civil law (French system) with customary law
legal_system.customary_law_role: Traditional chiefs mediate disputes; customary law for land/family in rural areas
legal_system.notes: 2024 constitutional amendment controversy (Fifth Republic, parliamentary system concentrating power); OHADA business law; Cour Constitutionnelle.

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global.
comparative_rankings.notes: Port of Lomé gives outsized economic importance; Gnassingbé dynasty among Africa's longest.

current_leader.name: Faure Gnassingbé
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: RPT/UNIR; son of Gnassingbé Eyadéma; succeeded father on his death; widely contested elections; constitutional changes 2024 to extend rule; Gnassingbé family has ruled since 1967

former_leaders.name: Sylvanus Olympio
former_leaders.notes: First president; Ewe; assassinated in Africa's first military coup (January 13, 1963); killed at US Embassy gates by Gnassingbé Eyadéma

former_leaders.name: Nicolas Grunitzky
former_leaders.notes: Installed after Olympio's assassination; overthrown by Eyadéma

former_leaders.name: Gnassingbé Eyadéma
former_leaders.notes: 38-year rule; Africa's longest-serving president at time of death; Kabiyé; RPT single party; personality cult; died in office February 2005; son Faure immediately installed

910.name: Indigenous Peoples of Togo
910.description: Early settlement of the Togo hills; Ewe, Kabye, Tem, and other peoples establish diverse societies.

sub_clusters.name: Early Settlement and Koutammakou
sub_clusters.description: Archaeological evidence of early habitation; Koutammakou region of Batammariba people; fortified tower-houses (takienta).

sub_clusters.name: Ewe, Kabye, and Tem Peoples
sub_clusters.description: Ewe migrations from Notsie; Kabye highland farming communities; Tem traders link forest and savanna.

920.name: Migrations and Early State Formation
920.description: Ewe migration from Notsie; Dagomba and other northern influence; decentralised political systems.

sub_clusters.name: Ewe Migration from Notsie
sub_clusters.description: Ewe oral tradition recounts exodus from Notsie under tyrannical king Agokoli; dispersal across southern Togo and Ghana.

sub_clusters.name: Northern Kingdoms and Dagomba Influence
sub_clusters.description: Dagomba, Tchokossi, and Bassar polities in northern Togo; iron smelting at Bassar; trans-regional trade.

930.name: Slave Coast Trade and Togo
930.description: Southern Togo as part of the Slave Coast; Aneho (Little Popo) and Agoué as trading centres; Danish, Dutch, and Portuguese factors.

sub_clusters.name: Little Popo (Aneho) Slave Trade
sub_clusters.description: Aneho as major slave-trading port; Mina and other groups mediate between European traders and interior.

sub_clusters.name: Coastal Commerce and European Presence
sub_clusters.description: Danish, Dutch, Portuguese, and later German traders; palm oil replaces slave trade; Agoué and coastal settlements.

sub_clusters.name: Dahomey Kingdom Influence
sub_clusters.description: Kingdom of Dahomey raids and influences eastern Togo; slave-raiding wars; Ewe buffer communities.

940.name: German Togoland
940.description: Gustav Nachtigal secures protectorate 1884; Musterkolonie (model colony); railway and cocoa; WWI conquest.

sub_clusters.name: Nachtigal Treaty and German Protectorate
sub_clusters.description: Gustav Nachtigal signs treaty with chief Mlapa III at Togoville 1884; Berlin Conference confirms German claim.

sub_clusters.name: Musterkolonie (Model Colony)
sub_clusters.description: Germans develop Togoland as showcase colony; railways, cocoa plantations, Lomé port; relatively less violent than other colonies.

sub_clusters.name: World War I Conquest of Togoland
sub_clusters.description: British and French forces conquer Togoland in first Allied victory of WWI (August 1914); territory partitioned.

940.name: French Mandate and Trust Territory
940.description: League of Nations mandate then UN Trust Territory under France; Ewe unification movement; path to independence.

sub_clusters.name: French Mandate Administration
sub_clusters.description: France administers eastern two-thirds of former Togoland; forced labour; cocoa and coffee economy.

sub_clusters.name: Ewe Unification Movement
sub_clusters.description: All-Ewe Conference demands reunification of Ewe people split between French Togo and British Gold Coast; UN plebiscites.

sub_clusters.name: Autonomy and Independence
sub_clusters.description: Autonomous Republic 1956; Nicolas Grunitzky PM; Sylvanus Olympio's CUT wins UN-supervised elections 1958.

950.name: Independence and Sylvanus Olympio
950.description: Independence 1960; Olympio's presidency; assassination 1963 in Africa's first military coup of the independence era; Grunitzky interlude.

sub_clusters.name: Independence of Togo
sub_clusters.description: Togo independent 27 April 1960; Sylvanus Olympio first president; refuses to integrate demobilised soldiers.

sub_clusters.name: Assassination of Sylvanus Olympio
sub_clusters.description: Sergeant Gnassingbé Eyadéma among soldiers who kill Olympio in coup 13 January 1963; Grunitzky installed as president.

sub_clusters.name: Grunitzky Interlude
sub_clusters.description: Nicolas Grunitzky presidency; instability; Eyadéma leads bloodless coup 1967; begins personal rule.

950.name: Gnassingbé Eyadéma Dynasty
950.description: Eyadéma rules Togo for 38 years—one of Africa's longest-serving leaders; RPT single party; cult of personality; democratic façade.

sub_clusters.name: Eyadéma's Single-Party Rule
sub_clusters.description: RPT as sole party; northern Kabye military dominance; cult of personality; phosphate economy.

sub_clusters.name: Democratic Struggle and 1991 National Conference
sub_clusters.description: Pro-democracy movement; Sovereign National Conference 1991; Eyadéma uses military to claw back power; democratic transition fails.

sub_clusters.name: Eyadéma's Late Rule and Death
sub_clusters.description: Rigged elections; opposition boycotts; EU sanctions; constitutional change to allow further terms; dies in office February 2005.

960.name: Faure Gnassingbé and Contemporary Togo
960.description: Faure Gnassingbé succeeds father in disputed succession; Gnassingbé family becomes Africa's longest ruling dynasty; protests; constitutional changes.

sub_clusters.name: Faure Gnassingbé's Disputed Succession
sub_clusters.description: Military installs Faure Gnassingbé immediately after Eyadéma's death; forced to hold elections; wins amid violence and fraud (~500 killed).

sub_clusters.name: Gnassingbé Consolidation of Power
sub_clusters.description: Faure re-elected 2010, 2015; limited reforms; opposition fragmented; EU re-engagement and sanctions cycles.

sub_clusters.name: 2017 Protest Movement
sub_clusters.description: Massive anti-dynasty protests demand return to 1992 constitution and term limits; government cracks down; constitutional referendum.

sub_clusters.name: Fifth Republic and Parliamentary Shift
sub_clusters.description: Controversial constitutional change to parliamentary system 2024; Gnassingbé family extends grip; opposition denounces as constitutional coup.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
